prompt_md: A drawer holds 10 black socks and 10 red socks, all loose. In the dark, how many socks must you take out to be sure you have a matching pair?
prompt_short: 10 black and 10 red socks, in the dark. Socks needed for a sure pair?
explain_intuition_md: Two socks can be different colours, but a third has to match one of them. You'd need 11 only to be sure of getting one sock of each colour.
explain_math_md: Pigeonhole: $3$ socks in $2$ colours put at least $\lceil 3/2 \rceil = 2$ socks in one colour.
